items.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: We opened Kelly’s Stables in New York. And those were swinging, like Pete Brown and Frankie, Eddie Doggerty on drums, Harry Prates on the bass and Ram Ramirez on piano.

ctx.x: When you moved to tenor sax —

Well I played with Frankie Newton in 1939, I was still playing clarinet. We opened Kelly’s Stables in New York. And those were swinging, like Pete Brown and Frankie, Eddie Doggerty on drums, Harry Prates on the bass and Ram Ramirez on piano. It was a swinging club. Everybody used to come in to the club. That’s when Coleman Hawkins came back from Europe in 1939 and ‘40. We opened it in 1940. In 1939 it was on 51st Street, and in 1940 he opened on 52nd Street, and we were the main band. items.q: But he started on clarinet with us.

ctx.x: Well, he had a lot. He had Flip Phillips.
That's the one. Before Flip Phillips, his name was Filipippo(?). He played clarinet with Frankie.
No, Flip never played anything but tenor.
